title: How to Clean Windows Without Streaks
hook: You wash your windows, and they dry with streaks, smears and cloudy patches. The mistake is in the method, not the cleaner. Seven steps to get glass crystal clear, inside and out, with simple supplies. Stay for step five: it's the move the professionals use.
intro: Streaks have three causes: cleaning in direct sun, so the liquid dries too fast; too much cleaner, which leaves a film; and the wrong cloth, which leaves lint. Fix those three, and a bucket and a squeegee are enough. Never lean out of upper-floor windows, or use a ladder without help.
youNeedNarration: You'll need a bucket of warm water, a drop of dish soap, a squeegee with a clean blade, microfiber cloths, and, if you like, white vinegar for spot cleaning.
heroImagePrompt: A spotless streak-free window with soft sunlight and green garden view, a squeegee and a bucket on the sill, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Pick the right time and gather supplies
steps.narration: Step one. Choose a cloudy day, or work in the shade, because direct sun dries the cleaner before you can wipe it, and leaves streaks. Avoid freezing weather, too. Gather all your supplies before you start, so you don't have to leave with wet hands. Lay a towel on the sill and floor to catch drips. Work on windows you can safely reach from the ground, indoors or outdoors. Open the window slightly if you want to clean the frame edges. Also, remove curtains, plants and ornaments from the sill beforehand, so nothing gets wet or knocked over.
steps.tip: Cloudy days give the best results
steps.imagePrompt: A bucket of soapy water, a squeegee and microfiber cloths on a windowsill with a towel, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Dust the frame and the glass
steps.narration: Step two. Use a dry brush or a vacuum with a soft attachment to remove cobwebs, dust and loose dirt from the frame, the sill and the corners. Wipe the edges of the glass with a dry cloth. If you skip this, the water will turn the dust to muddy streaks that run down the glass. Take a moment to clear the window track too, where dirt collects. Cleaning from the top down avoids dripping on cleaned areas. This takes two minutes, but it makes the whole job much cleaner and prevents you from smearing dirt. Next comes the cleaning solution, and it needs less soap than you might think.
steps.imagePrompt: A soft brush sweeping dust from a white window frame and sill, bright light, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Mix a simple cleaning solution
steps.narration: Step three. Fill a bucket with about a gallon, or four litres, of warm water, and add just a few drops of dish soap. Less is better. Too much soap leaves a film that causes streaks. For a spray-bottle alternative, mix equal parts water and white vinegar. This works well on lightly dirty glass. Avoid vinegar on natural stone sills, and test it on rubber seals. Never mix vinegar with bleach or ammonia. Some people add a splash of rubbing alcohol in winter, which helps the glass dry quickly in cold weather.
steps.tip: Just a few drops of soap
steps.imagePrompt: A bucket of warm water with a few soap bubbles and a sponge beside it on a windowsill, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Wash the glass
steps.narration: Step four. Dip a microfiber cloth or a sponge-and-scrubber tool into the solution, and wring it out lightly. Wipe the whole pane from top to bottom, using firm strokes to lift dirt. Pay attention to the corners and edges, where grime collects. For stubborn spots like bird droppings, hold the wet cloth on the spot for a minute to soften them. Don't use abrasive scrubbers on glass, which can cause scratches. Keep the glass wet until you squeegee. If the window is very dirty, wash it twice, because the first pass lifts the heavy dirt and the second gets the rest. Now for the squeegee, the step that makes the difference.
steps.tip: Keep the glass wet until you squeegee
steps.mistake: Letting the soapy water dry on the glass
steps.imagePrompt: A hand washing a large window pane with a wet sponge, soapy water running, bright daylight, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Squeegee in clean strokes
steps.narration: Step five. Start at the top corner, and pull the squeegee down in one straight stroke, or use a gentle S-shape across the glass. Wipe the rubber blade with a clean cloth after every pass. Overlap each stroke by an inch. Leave a small strip at the bottom, and wipe the final line with a cloth. A clean, sharp rubber blade is key to a perfect result. If the blade is cracked or worn, replace it. Practise on a small window first. The motion feels natural after a few strokes, and the results look professional.
steps.tip: Wipe the blade after every stroke
steps.mistake: Using a dirty or nicked rubber blade
steps.imagePrompt: A squeegee pulling a clean stroke down a wet window pane, leaving a clear path, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Dry the edges and polish
steps.narration: Step six. Use a dry microfiber cloth to wipe the edges of the glass, the frame and the sill, where water gathers. Then polish any drops or marks on the pane with another dry, lint-free cloth. For an inside window, use a light touch. Avoid paper towels and newspaper, which leave lint, or ink. Step back and look at the glass from an angle, and from outside and inside, to spot any streaks. A damp cloth then removes any final smudges. Always check both sides of the glass, because streaks may be on the other side. One step is left, and it covers the parts people forget.
steps.tip: Check from an angle in the light
steps.mistake: Wiping with paper towels that leave lint
steps.imagePrompt: A hand buffing the corner of a clean window pane with a dry microfiber cloth, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Clean the tracks and screens
steps.narration: Step seven. Finish with the parts people forget. Vacuum the window track, then wipe it with a cloth dipped in warm soapy water. A cotton swab or a toothbrush reaches the corners. Remove the screens, and rinse them gently with a hose, or brush them with soapy water, then let them dry before replacing them. Then wipe the sills and frames. Clean windows every three to four months, or when they look dull, and the job will remain quick. A quick wipe once a month stops dirt from building up, and makes the next big clean much faster.
steps.tip: Clean the screens and the tracks too
steps.mistake: Putting wet screens back in the frame
steps.imagePrompt: A toothbrush cleaning dust from a window track with a vacuum nozzle nearby, photorealistic, no text

bonus.label: NOT WORKING?
bonus.title: Still streaky? Find the cause
bonus.narration: If streaks remain, work out which side they are on. Wipe the inside with horizontal strokes and the outside with vertical strokes. The direction of a streak then tells you which side to fix. Streaks usually mean too much soap, a dirty blade or cloth, or hard water. For hard water spots, wipe with a cloth dampened with white vinegar and water. Do not wash microfiber cloths with fabric softener, because it leaves a film.
bonus.imagePrompt: A window pane with faint streaks visible in low sunlight, a hand holding a microfiber cloth ready to wipe, bright room behind. Photorealistic photograph for a home how-to video. Bright, tidy home interior, soft daylight. Adult hands, no face visible. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

bonus.label: CALL A PRO
bonus.title: When to call a professional
bonus.narration: Some windows are better left to professionals. Upper-floor windows, and any glass you can only reach by leaning out, are a fall risk. Fog or moisture trapped between the two panes of a double-pane window means the seal has failed, and cleaning cannot fix it. Paint overspray and etching from hard water also need an expert's tools. A pro can tell you whether the glass can be saved.
bonus.tip: Fog between panes needs a pro
bonus.imagePrompt: A professional window cleaner in work clothes on a ladder wiping a large upper-floor window of a house with a squeegee, seen from the garden. Photorealistic photograph for a home how-to video. Bright, tidy home interior, soft daylight. Adult hands, no face visible. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

bonus.label: KEEP IT CLEAN
bonus.title: Keep windows clear longer
bonus.narration: A few habits keep glass clear longer. Wipe fingerprints and smudges right away with a damp microfiber cloth. Wash your cloths without fabric softener, and let them air dry. Clean the glass a couple of times a year, and the screens and tracks at the same time. Wipe away condensation on cold mornings, so mold does not start. Keep a small squeegee near the bathroom window for quick wipes.
bonus.imagePrompt: A spotless large window flooding a living room with sunlight, a folded microfiber cloth and a small squeegee on the windowsill. Photorealistic photograph for a home how-to video. Bright, tidy home interior, soft daylight. Adult hands, no face visible. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

mistakesToAvoid.narration: Here are the mistakes to avoid. First, cleaning in direct sunlight. The liquid dries before you can wipe, and the sun gives you streaks. Second, using too much soap or cleaner. A little is enough, and more only leaves a film. And third, using dirty cloths or a dirty squeegee blade. They spread dirt, rather than lifting it. For upper floors, hire a professional or use a proper extension pole, and never lean out of a window. Be careful with glass edges and ladders, and ask for help whenever you can.
items: Using too much soap or cleaner

recap.narration: Let's recap. Pick the right time, and gather your supplies. Dust the frame and the glass. Mix a simple solution with just a little soap. Wash the glass. Squeegee in clean strokes. Dry the edges and polish. And clean the tracks and screens. Seven steps, about an hour for a whole house, and windows that let the light in. Bonus sections cover how to track down stubborn streaks, when to call a professional, and how to keep windows clear longer.
items: Pick the right time and gather supplies
Dust the frame and the glass

outro: That's how you clean windows without streaks, inside and out. If your windows are sparkling, subscribe to WikiTube, because we publish a new how-to every single day. Tell us in the comments what you want us to clean next, and see you tomorrow.

metadata.title: How to Clean Windows Without Streaks (It's Your Method, Not the Cleaner)
metadata.description:
Streaky windows? In this step-by-step video you'll learn how to clean windows without streaks, inside and out: pick the right time, dust the frames, mix a simple solution with a few drops of dish soap, wash the glass, squeegee in clean strokes, dry and polish the edges, and clean the tracks and screens. Easy, cheap and safe for ground-floor windows, with no special products needed.

You'll need: a bucket of warm water, a drop of dish soap, a squeegee, microfiber cloths, white vinegar (optional).

Fácil, barato y seguro para ventanas de planta baja.

hi.description:

it.title: Come pulire le finestre senza aloni (dentro e fuori)
it.description:
Le tue finestre si asciugano con strisce e aloni? In questo video passo passo scopri come pulire le finestre senza aloni, dentro e fuori: scegliere il momento giusto, spolverare i telai, preparare una soluzione semplice con poche gocce di detersivo per piatti, lavare il vetro, passare il tergivetro con movimenti netti, asciugare e lucidare i bordi e pulire binari e zanzariere. Facile, economico e sicuro per le finestre al piano terra.
